name: Mežaparks
description: Mezaparks is one of the most beautiful, greenest, and also one of the most prestigious neighbourhoods in Riga, as well as a popular recreation area. The major cultural and recreational park Mezaparks opened in 1949. One of the few remaining forested areas in Riga became integral part of the park and gave it its identity. The Mežaparks Grand Bandstand is where Latvia sings at full volume. Since 1955, it has been the home of the Latvian Song Celebration – every five years, choirs, dancers and audiences gather here, turning Mežaparks into one huge shared moment.

name: Freedom Monument
description:
The Freedom Monument is one of Latvia’s strongest symbols of independence – a place where Riga’s heart beats especially loud.
In 2023, two world records were set at the foot of the monument during the World Athletics Road Running Championships Riga23. The women’s road mile world record, 4:20.98, still stands today.

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
description: The Latvian National Museum of Art is one of Riga’s key cultural stops. Its main building, opened in 1905, was the first purpose-built art museum building in the Baltics.

name: Riga Castle
description:
Riga Castle, on the bank of the Daugava, is the official residence of the President of Latvia and one of Riga’s oldest landmarks.
Look up at the tower — if the white President’s flag is flying, the President is working in the Castle. Spot it on race day as you head down the finish straight!

name: Vanšu Bridge
description:
Vanšu Bridge is one of Riga’s most recognisable lines across the Daugava – with its tall pylon, cables and wide views towards Ķīpsala.
It connects the city centre with Pārdaugava and is one of those spots where Riga looks especially photogenic on marathon day.

name: Stone Bridge
description:
The Stone Bridge is one of Riga’s classic views — across the Daugava towards Old Riga and its skyline of church towers.
Long before today’s bridge, this crossing was home to earlier raft and pontoon bridges. The current bridge opened in 1957.

name: National Library of Latvia
description:
The National Library of Latvia, also known as the Castle of Light, resembles a "glass mountain" from Latvian folklore.
The building holds Latvia’s stories, books and knowledge – and offers a great view back towards Riga.
